Refinement-DAG Software Development

Formal Technical Report · November 2026 · Refinement-DAG Software Development: A Calculus of Verified Behavior Inclusions for Agent-Authored Systems
💡 Collaborative Review & Inline Annotations: Select any sentence, theorem, or formula in the text to pop up the "💬 Annotate selection" button — save locally, copy as Markdown, or publish directly as a shared GitHub Issue annotation anchored to the passage.
⬇ Download PDF
⬇ Download PDF

Abstract

Section titled “Abstract”

Agent-authored software requires a principled boundary between the behavioral guarantees it must preserve and the internal implementation details an automated agent is permitted to change. The development method presented here serves five root purposes: realizing committed behavior, preserving authority over governing meaning, keeping justified change local, reducing the context required for human governance, and keeping assurance accountable to evidence. Its compositional theorems concern finite visible-trace safety, relating local component machines, parent-owned contracts, executable leaves, and architectural connectors through five distinct inclusion roles. Three chosen operational disciplines make system boundaries unambiguous: Restricted Leaf Normal Form (pure, terminating handlers over state-indexed enabled inputs); letter-or-erasure trace observations paired with deterministic protocol monitors; and single-owner stateful runtime instances, allowing sharing without replication only for genuinely state-free definitions. A guarded, execution-witness-indexed wiring obligation bridges local verification to concrete composition, establishing conditional root soundness, the soundness of root-covering inspection frontiers, and an incremental frame theorem for exact-operand evidence reuse.

Separate operational obligations cover required reception and readiness; selected response duties additionally rule out silent loss and boundary-owned non-progress while permitting declared, inspectable external waits. A complete durable-acknowledgement example distinguishes these safety and progress claims and makes their explicit runtime premises transparent. Interactive inspection and context-limited intent authoring are formulated as governance requirements; no empirical reduction in human effort is claimed.

1. Introduction

Section titled “1. Introduction”

When software is authored or modified by autonomous agents, an agent can make a failing test suite pass by repairing the implementation, by weakening test assertions, or by altering the underlying meaning of the requirement. Only the first constitutes a genuine implementation repair. A sound development method must distinguish these actions before a successful tool invocation can be accepted as verification evidence. We adopt a cooperative-fallibility baseline: agents and developers are assumed to act without adversarial malice, but their proposals are fallible, prone to scope creep, and liable to introduce subtle regressions or false abstractions unless checked against formal boundaries.

The same distinction governs system composition. A storage subsystem may satisfy its local component model while that model permits acknowledgement prior to durable persistence. Conversely, a correct implementation may fail refinement simply because its abstraction admits environment executions that cannot occur in deployment. Neither failure mode is resolved by adding reviewers to an informal boundary. The specification, the abstraction, the executable implementation, and the evidence claim must be maintained as distinct, first-class objects.

To establish these boundaries, the development method is organized around five root purposes:

  • P1: Realize committed behavior. Actual whole-system execution must satisfy accepted promises under their declared operational conditions; required operating conditions cannot be excluded merely to make verification succeed.
  • P2: Preserve authority over governing meaning. The adoption, modification, and retirement of governing commitments must be authorized by entitled stakeholders or an applicable delegation; implementation authority does not confer authority to rewrite system requirements.
  • P3: Keep justified change local. When an implementation or environment changes, previously established guarantees and evidence are reused whenever their validity conditions survive. Locality is conditional on evidence applicability, not an unconstrained property of every source edit.
  • P4: Reduce human governance context. The system representation must minimize the extraneous detail a human must hold in working memory. During upstream intent authoring, stakeholders express or revise intent using decision-relevant responsibilities and interfaces without reconstructing unrelated leaf code or proof scripts. During downstream assessment, interactive visual inspection exposes commitments, boundaries, changes, unresolved duties, and external dependencies without concealing qualifications that could alter an architectural decision.
  • P5: Keep assurance accountable to evidence. Every claim must be bound to its identified subject, assumptions, and supporting artifacts; commitments, open questions, empirical observations, and refutable hypotheses remain strictly distinguished.

To realize these purposes, the calculus developed here uses one finite-safety relation—set inclusion of finite visible traces—across five distinct typed roles: satisfaction, wiring adequacy, decomposition, child refinement, and leaf realization. Their operands are not interchangeable. In particular, a parent proves its architectural design against abstract contracts, whereas an executable connector is proved sound for operational witnesses that satisfy those contracts. A development DAG records these obligations and their provenance without allowing obligation activation to depend on proof success.

Systems admitted to this calculus obey three orthogonal operational disciplines:

  • O1: Restricted Leaf Normal Form (RLNF). A leaf consists of pure, terminating, explicit-state handlers δℓ\delta_\ellδℓ​, defined over state-indexed enabled inputs enℓ(s)\mathrm{en}_\ell(s)enℓ​(s). Each handler returns a finite list of emitted outputs. Substrate operations are modeled as command events; their asynchronous results arrive as response inputs.
  • O2: Homomorphic observation and deterministic contract monitors. Each edge observation is induced by a letter-or-erasure action map. A Level-3 contract is a deterministic, single-initial, prefix-closed protocol monitor. These restrictions guarantee an exact equivalence between trace inclusion and relational forward simulation.
  • O3: Single-owner stateful instances / state-free sharing. Every stateful runtime instance has at most one owning parent boundary, which strictly routes and mediates all client access. Definitions with a single semantic state and no hidden mutable state may be shared across multiple parents in the DAG. In contrast, separate runtime instances of a stateful definition possess distinct runtime identities and disjoint owned mutable state.

These operational principles are chosen design disciplines of the calculus rather than unique mathematical consequences of P1–P5. They establish orthogonal language, observation, and ownership foundations. To prevent unsolicited outputs, hidden shared aliases, or trivial input refusal (such as producing only the empty trace ϵ\epsilonϵ), the calculus enforces explicit delivery, confinement, relative input receptiveness, and evidence applicability obligations at each system boundary. Furthermore, to eliminate silent hangs and uninspected stalling, selected boundaries enforce duty-relative readiness and non-silent response conditions that permit declared, inspectable external waits without weakening terminal commitments.

The contributions of this work are:

  1. The restricted operational semantics and five-place refinement algebra;
  2. A guarded, witness-indexed composition theorem;
  3. Conditional DAG and frontier soundness theorems;
  4. Protected-boundary versioned evolution with exact-operand proof reuse (an incremental frame theorem and interface cutoff corollary);
  5. A fully instantiated, end-to-end durable-acknowledgement example with discriminating counterexamples; and
  6. A contract-relative non-silent response condition that distinguishes permitted terminal outcomes from genuine external waits, with a separate readiness and progress argument for the worked example.

Sections 2–4 define the finite-safety algebra, the development DAG record, and the separate reception, readiness, and non-silent response obligations. Sections 5–7 address composition, human-governed development protocols, and evidence-preserving evolution. Section 8 details the durable-acknowledgement case study, its safety proof, its scoped progress argument, and discriminating regressions. Sections 9–11 review related work, discuss fundamental limitations, and conclude. Appendix A provides expanded mathematical proofs; Appendix B summarizes formal notation.

An interface XXX has a disjoint action signature

tr⁡(M)={vis⁡(ρ)∣ρ is a finite execution of M}⊆(ΣXvis)∗.\operatorname{tr}(M)=\{\operatorname{vis}(\rho)\mid\rho\text{ is a finite execution of }M\}\subseteq(\Sigma_X^{\mathrm{vis}})^*.tr(M)={vis(ρ)∣ρ is a finite execution of M}⊆(ΣXvis​)∗.

Write ϵ\epsilonϵ for the empty word, u⪯tu\preceq tu⪯t for word-prefix order, and pref⁡L={u∣∃t∈L, u⪯t}\operatorname{pref}L=\{u\mid\exists t\in L,\ u\preceq t\}prefL={u∣∃t∈L, u⪯t} for prefix closure. A specification is an arbitrary language Φ⊆(ΣXvis)∗\Phi\subseteq(\Sigma_X^{\mathrm{vis}})^*Φ⊆(ΣXvis​)∗, whereas every operational machine trace language is non-empty, contains ϵ\epsilonϵ, and is closed under prefixes.

We adopt the action partition of Lynch and Tuttle (1989), but do not assume their global input-enabledness. Our open-interface admission rule is relative to a declared protocol (§2.5). Denotational behavior sets QQQ and operational execution witnesses NNN are kept distinct: Q=tr⁡(N)Q=\operatorname{tr}(N)Q=tr(N) abstracts away state spaces, input acceptance, ownership, and runtime scheduling structure. Concrete composition plugs in operational witnesses NNN, rather than unstructured sets of words.

Finite visible traces record which finite sequences of visible events can occur. They do not record refusal, whether an execution terminates or continues forever, or whether a duty remains permanently pending. Operational obligations introduced below evaluate the operational execution witness NNN and its declared runtime interpretation directly, rather than attempting to recover liveness, readiness, or divergence distinctions from the trace language.

Inverse-image notation is deliberately distinct from the star denoting word extension.

The calculus admits four levels of contract precision. They describe choices of predicates, not four different refinement relations.

Level Contract meaning What evidence must establish
0: Top ⊤\top⊤ Every well-typed finite trace Inclusion is trivial; no nontrivial protocol guarantee follows.
1: Type/shape Every recorded value or event has the required shape A sound typing or schema argument for the selected observation; a compiler invocation alone is insufficient without its soundness and language assumptions.
2: Pre/post For completed calls, P(x)⇒Q(x,y)P(x)\Rightarrow Q(x,y)P(x)⇒Q(x,y); behavior outside PPP is unconstrained A sound Hoare-style argument. A completed-call relation alone does not establish termination, initialization, input acceptance, or feasibility.
3: Protocol A deterministic partial monitor admitting all prefixes of its runs A trace-inclusion proof or the initialized simulation of §4.3, together with separate admission checks.

Levels 1 and 2 lift directly to trace predicates by evaluating completed request-response pairs. Following the feasibility foundations of Unifying Theories of Programming (Woodcock and Cavalcanti, 2004), specifications require explicit operational witnesses to ensure that preconditions are satisfiable and models are non-empty. In this setting, RLNF establishes totality and termination for each enabled handler over its declared enabled state-input domain. Environmental feasibility and the satisfiability of required uses are verified separately; an uninvoked partial branch with unsatisfiable preconditions (P=falseP=\mathrm{false}P=false) remains a valid partial-correctness specification for unused operations.

These precision levels describe safety meanings and their associated verification evidence. None of these levels alone implies required input reception, operational readiness, or eventual response. A monitor encoding may represent a coarser safety predicate without altering its language; neither an artificial level tag nor an independent verifier is mathematically required.

The bridge between this operational composition and the denotational transformer KvK_vKv​ is established by the guarded wiring obligation in Condition 5 (§3.4).

The five obligations form a coherent algebraic inclusion chain, establishing compositional finite-safety properties. Operational delivery and admission supply its essential execution premises. Required input reception, operational readiness, and scoped non-silent response are additional behavioral properties of the admitted execution witnesses; they are not consequences of language inclusion alone.

2.5 Semantic profile scope, reception, readiness, and non-silent response

Section titled “2.5 Semantic profile scope, reception, readiness, and non-silent response”

The finite-safety profile Γsafe\Gamma_{\mathrm{safe}}Γsafe​ fixes finite visible traces, prefix-closed inclusion, the action partition, and operational admission, ensuring that initialization is non-empty, state invariants hold, and accepted environmental contexts admit feasible physical realizations.

To eliminate silent drops, uninspected hangs, and enabled-but-untaken continuations, boundaries with response commitments enforce three additional operational obligations: relative input reception, operational readiness, and contract-relative non-silent response.

2.5.1 Relative input reception is configuration-sensitive

Section titled “2.5.1 Relative input reception is configuration-sensitive”

Relative input receptiveness is checked across reachable concrete configurations, not merely by examining visible trace words. For a deterministic visible protocol monitor BBB and a concrete finite execution ρ\rhoρ of witness NNN, let

s=last⁡(ρ),h=πin(vis⁡(ρ)),q=β^(q0,λ∗(vis⁡(ρ))).s=\operatorname{last}(\rho),\qquad h=\pi_{\mathrm{in}}(\operatorname{vis}(\rho)),\qquad q=\widehat\beta(q_0,\lambda^*(\operatorname{vis}(\rho))).s=last(ρ),h=πin​(vis(ρ)),q=β​(q0​,λ∗(vis(ρ))).

At every reachable in-scope configuration and history (s,h)(s,h)(s,h), each protocol-permitted concrete input iii satisfying hi∈Ahi \in Ahi∈A must have an enabled acceptance transition s→is′s \xrightarrow{i} s'si​s′ in the concrete machine.

When inputs are mapped or erased under homomorphism λ\lambdaλ, the boundary declaration specifies their concrete acceptance relation; hidden response protocols remain explicit. A pending-output state cannot waive a permitted input through an arbitrary internal readiness flag. Either the corresponding protocol state forbids the input, or a modeled input arrival buffer must accept it. Two executions with identical visible traces may reach different internal configurations; relative reception requires acceptance at all reachable configurations corresponding to that protocol state.

2.5.2 Duties, permitted outcomes, and genuine external waits

Section titled “2.5.2 Duties, permitted outcomes, and genuine external waits”

For each boundary carrying an accepted response commitment, an accepted request occurrence opens a duty ddd. Duties are tracked by occurrence identity, avoiding the need for bureaucratic authorization tokens. Evaluated over the concrete runtime configuration enriched by necessary correlation history:

  • PdP_dPd​: the duty is outstanding. It becomes true upon request acceptance and remains true until a permitted terminal outcome for that occurrence is observed at the promising boundary.
  • DdD_dDd​: a permitted terminal outcome for duty ddd is emitted at the promising boundary. Success and failure outcomes count toward DdD_dDd​ only under their contractually declared conditions. Emitting an internal outcome at an intermediate child boundary does not discharge the parent’s duty.
  • Wd,eW_{d,e}Wd,e​: duty ddd is genuinely blocked on an unresolved external prerequisite occurrence or condition eee, and the wait is accurately inspectable. Wd,eW_{d,e}Wd,e​ strictly implies PdP_dPd​.

The predicate Wd,eW_{d,e}Wd,e​ is a factual causal condition, not an arbitrary state annotation:

  1. External prerequisite: eee is an actual outstanding event or condition outside the realization and scheduling authority of this boundary.
  2. Causal dependency: Under the accepted contract and current conditions, the next step necessary to advance duty ddd depends on eee, and no boundary-owned action is presently due instead. An already available result, an undrained pending output, a required failure diagnostic, or a runnable internal continuation cannot be concealed as an external wait.
  3. Accurate inspectability: The identity of duty ddd, the responsible boundary, the external prerequisite eee, and known status/uncertainty are exposed for external or human inspection. A specialized UI schema or root-cause verifier is not mandated.
  4. Resolution invalidation: Once eee resolves, Wd,eW_{d,e}Wd,e​ ceases to hold. A subsequent retry or new external request creates a distinct prerequisite occurrence and cannot retroactively reuse an old wait explanation.

At a composite parent boundary, all child components, internal connectors, and owned scheduling queues lie inside the realization. Consequently, a child waiting for a sibling component is an internal dependency of the parent, not a parent external wait. A parent may expose a genuine external prerequisite reached through its children (such as an unresolved storage flush), but internal sibling ping-pong remains owned work.

The interpretation of duties and permitted outcomes derives entirely from the accepted contract. It is not inferred from private state names such as Done, nor from whether an internal handler returns an empty output list. Pure input-only operations that carry no response promise define no response duty.

Each accepted contract declares a wait policy Ed∞E_d^\inftyEd∞​, representing the set of external prerequisite occurrences or conditions at which duty ddd is permitted to remain pending indefinitely. For a strict terminal-response contract, Ed∞=∅E_d^\infty = \emptysetEd∞​=∅. The predicate Wd,eW_{d,e}Wd,e​ may hold during legitimate transient waiting for such a duty; genuine waiting does not itself grant permission to hang indefinitely. Conversely, permission to wait indefinitely does not fabricate a prerequisite where none exists.

2.5.3 Operational readiness (Ready\mathrm{Ready}Ready)

Section titled “2.5.3 Operational readiness (Ready\mathrm{Ready}Ready)”

Let the duty-relative transition relation be defined as a restriction of the actual transition relation:

s→owned(d)s′⟺∃a. s→as′ ∧ Owned⁡v(s,a,s′) ∧ Continuation⁡d(s,a,s′).s \xrightarrow{\mathrm{owned}(d)} s' \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \exists a.\ s \xrightarrow{a} s' \ \land\ \operatorname{Owned}_v(s,a,s') \ \land\ \operatorname{Continuation}_d(s,a,s').sowned(d)​s′⟺∃a. sa​s′ ∧ Ownedv​(s,a,s′) ∧ Continuationd​(s,a,s′).

Here Owned⁡v\operatorname{Owned}_vOwnedv​ classifies internal computation, dispatch, routing, or output steps belonging to boundary vvv, and Continuation⁡d\operatorname{Continuation}_dContinuationd​ asserts that the transition advances duty ddd along an admitted path. This classification must be justified from the actual implementation witness; it cannot be asserted by fiat or treat unrelated background activity as progress toward ddd.

Required readiness is:

∀s reachable, d.Pd(s)∧¬∃e Wd,e(s) ⟹ ∃s′. s→owned(d)s′.(Ready)\forall s \text{ reachable},\ d.\quad P_d(s) \land \neg\exists e\, W_{d,e}(s) \ \Longrightarrow\ \exists s'.\ s \xrightarrow{\mathrm{owned}(d)} s'. \tag{Ready}∀s reachable, d.Pd​(s)∧¬∃eWd,e​(s) ⟹ ∃s′. sowned(d)​s′.(Ready)

Readiness ensures that whenever a duty is outstanding and not blocked on an inspectable external prerequisite, an owned continuation step is enabled. Intermediate internal computation is permitted; the formula does not demand that every pending state immediately emit a terminal output.

2.5.4 Complete-execution non-silent response (NS\mathrm{NS}NS)

Section titled “2.5.4 Complete-execution non-silent response (NS\mathrm{NS}NS)”

Let CExec⁡v(Nv,ω)\operatorname{CExec}_v(N_v,\omega)CExecv​(Nv​,ω) denote the maximal executions of the declared runtime semantics at boundary vvv, subject to stated execution premises. The runtime semantics accounts for internal computation, scheduling, delay steps, external waiting, and quiescence. Finite maximal (quiescent) executions are extended by idle stuttering for temporal evaluation; infinite executions are maximal by definition. Arbitrary truncated observation prefixes are not complete executions.

For every duty ddd committed by the contract:

NS⁡v(Nv) ⟺ ∀π∈CExec⁡v(Nv,ω), ∀d.π⊨G(Pd ⇒ [FDd ∨ ∃e∈Ed∞. FGWd,e]).(NS)\operatorname{NS}_v(N_v) \ \Longleftrightarrow\ \forall\pi\in\operatorname{CExec}_v(N_v,\omega),\ \forall d.\quad \pi \models \mathbf{G}\left(P_d \ \Rightarrow\ \left[\mathbf{F} D_d \ \lor\ \exists e\in E_d^\infty.\,\mathbf{F}\mathbf{G} W_{d,e}\right]\right). \tag{NS}NSv​(Nv​) ⟺ ∀π∈CExecv​(Nv​,ω), ∀d.π⊨G(Pd​ ⇒ [FDd​ ∨ ∃e∈Ed∞​.FGWd,e​]).(NS)

Here F\mathbf{F}F denotes eventually and G\mathbf{G}G denotes globally along execution path π\piπ. The second disjunct requires that the execution eventually settle into a persistent genuine external wait eee that belongs to the contract-permitted set Ed∞E_d^\inftyEd∞​. In this selected profile, placing ∃e∈Ed∞\exists e\in E_d^\infty∃e∈Ed∞​ outside FG\mathbf{F}\mathbf{G}FG requires an unresolved execution to stabilize at one specific external prerequisite instance rather than cycling among transient waits; services whose contracts admit unbounded external retry polling require a corresponding multi-wait progress profile.

The consequences of NS\mathrm{NS}NS are precise:

  • A permitted terminal outcome discharges the duty. A persistent external wait does not discharge it; rather, the accepted contract permits that unresolved execution only at a declared member of Ed∞E_d^\inftyEd∞​.
  • An implementation that accepts a request and transitions to Done with an empty output list without emitting a required outcome or entering an external wait fails both Ready\mathrm{Ready}Ready and NS\mathrm{NS}NS.
  • An execution trapped in an internal loop while a terminal outcome remains enabled fails NS\mathrm{NS}NS, even if safety, reception, and readiness hold.
  • A permanently unresolved external prerequisite (such as an indefinite disk flush), accurately inspectable and with no withheld owned work, satisfies NS\mathrm{NS}NS if and only if e∈Ed∞e \in E_d^\inftye∈Ed∞​.
  • For a strict contract (Ed∞=∅E_d^\infty = \emptysetEd∞​=∅), transient external waiting is permitted by Ready\mathrm{Ready}Ready, but NS\mathrm{NS}NS demands FDd\mathbf{F} D_dFDd​; if the external result never arrives, NS\mathrm{NS}NS fails. Inspectability does not excuse failure to deliver a promised terminal response.
  • Once an external prerequisite resolves, lingering at the old wait state or starving subsequent output drains violates NS\mathrm{NS}NS.
  • Periodic cycling through transient wait labels without permanently remaining at an unresolved prerequisite fails the second disjunct FGWd,e\mathbf{F}\mathbf{G} W_{d,e}FGWd,e​.

Operational obligations Ready\mathrm{Ready}Ready and NS\mathrm{NS}NS apply where response duties are explicitly declared. A safety-only boundary is not silently upgraded to a terminal-response service, and finite prefixes stopping after request reception remain valid safety observations.

2.6 Boundary discipline

Section titled “2.6 Boundary discipline”

Component contracts specify visible interactions—enabled inputs, emitted outputs, response duties, permitted failure conditions, acknowledgements, causal ordering, and client preconditions—while preserving encapsulation of internal algorithms, data structures, and execution policies. A contract may specify which external prerequisites are admitted as persistent waits (Ed∞E_d^\inftyEd∞​) and what ordering or acknowledgement duties the caller must satisfy. It must not prescribe a consumer’s unrelated internal policies or scheduling strategies.

The parent boundary defines the slot contract, and the child component establishes compliance through its chosen internal realization. RLNF serves as an operational admission standard for verified handlers, guaranteeing termination and explicit state transitions on enabled inputs without constraining unrelated component design choices. Implementation-specific proof artifacts, such as internal inductive ranks or termination measures, are evidence supplied by a component, not obligations imposed on caller contracts.

The development record explicitly decouples obligation definitions from their verification status: III tracks formal intents with stable identities, unique owners, scoped predicates ⟦j⟧\llbracket j\rrbracket[[j]], and authority tags (root, protected, or delegated). The support mapping J(j)J(j)J(j) defines finite collections of conjunctive support groups, where alternative groups represent disjunctive proof paths over an acyclic support-reference graph. Operational duty and execution interpretations are maintained directly within the semantic profile of M(v)\mathcal M(v)M(v), avoiding redundant parallel ledgers. Stateful runtime instances and stateless reusable definitions are partitioned according to the single-owner discipline of §3.5.

Φ(v)=⋂j∈A(v)⟦j⟧,\Phi(v)=\bigcap_{j\in A(v)}\llbracket j\rrbracket,Φ(v)=⋂j∈A(v)​[[j]],

Lemma 2 (Evidence Separation). AAA depends only on I,JI,JI,J, not on EEE.

The authored support groups explain why an obligation is active within the development record; they neither prove its behavioral correctness nor require an exhaustive enumeration of all possible minimal supports. Each active behavioral claim must still be discharged by applicable verification evidence.

3.5 Edge refinement and the single-owner discipline

Section titled “3.5 Edge refinement and the single-owner discipline”

Every edge satisfies

Tv,c(tr⁡(Mc))⊆tr⁡(Bv,c),T_{v,c}(\operatorname{tr}(M_c))\subseteq\operatorname{tr}(B_{v,c}),Tv,c​(tr(Mc​))⊆tr(Bv,c​),

or the corresponding coarse slot predicate. Incoming edges to a shared definition have separate abstractions, input scopes, and contracts; each must be checked.

For a stateful runtime instance ccc, ∣par⁡(c)∣≤1|\operatorname{par}(c)|\le1∣par(c)∣≤1. All access crosses its owning parent connector, and there is no cross-branch hidden alias to its state or mutable substrate. A reusable stateful definition may be instantiated more than once, but its instances have distinct identities and disjoint owned mutable state. A definition shared without replication is state-free only if ∣Sc∣=1|S_c|=1∣Sc​∣=1 and its complete semantic closure, including descendants and substrate dependencies, has no mutable state. A composite owning a stateful descendant is therefore stateful for this rule. An effectful wrapper around a shared connection is not state-free merely because its source-level object has no fields. Runtime queues and pending-output buffers also have owners; sharing a pure handler definition does not share its invocation buffers.

Single-Parent Enclosure Lemma. Under this ownership and access discipline, every interaction with a stateful instance is enclosed by its unique parent boundary (or its external root boundary), and its ownership ancestry is a chain.

Proof. A non-root instance has one immediate owner. Every legal access crosses that owner by the access discipline. Repeating the owner relation yields at most one next ancestor at each step; acyclicity makes the sequence finite. Thus two purported independent owner paths cannot diverge above the instance, and an interaction from elsewhere must enter through the owning boundary rather than an alias. □\square□

The Single-Parent Enclosure Lemma establishes the exact architectural boundary where aggregate client interactions must be verified, ensuring that all access paths are mediated by the owning parent; it locates the boundary responsible for interactions rather than proving absence of deadlock or eventual progress by itself.

3.7 Subgraph extraction, root-covering cuts, and frontier soundness

Section titled “3.7 Subgraph extraction, root-covering cuts, and frontier soundness”

For S⊆VS\subseteq VS⊆V, let Anc⁡(S)\operatorname{Anc}(S)Anc(S) and Desc⁡(S)\operatorname{Desc}(S)Desc(S) be reflexive ancestor and descendant closures. The interval from uuu to www is Desc⁡({u})∩Anc⁡({w})\operatorname{Desc}(\{u\})\cap\operatorname{Anc}(\{w\})Desc({u})∩Anc({w}). A root-covering cut FFF is an antichain intersecting every root-to-leaf path. These are semantic inspection boundaries, not graph-layout levels; different branches may meet FFF at different depths.

For v∈Anc⁡(F)v\in\operatorname{Anc}(F)v∈Anc(F) define

UF(v)={tr⁡(Mv),v∈F,Kv((Tv,c(UF(c)))c),v∉F.U_F(v)=\begin{cases} \operatorname{tr}(M_v),&v\in F,\\ K_v((T_{v,c}(U_F(c)))_c),&v\notin F. \end{cases}UF​(v)={tr(Mv​),Kv​((Tv,c​(UF​(c)))c​),​v∈F,v∈/F.​

This recursion is well typed. If vvv is above the cut and one child had no descendant in FFF, extending that child path to a leaf would bypass FFF; an earlier cut ancestor would contradict the antichain property. Thus all required children are in the upper region. Shared state-free nodes are evaluated once with their edge-indexed transformers.

Corollary 1 (Frontier Soundness). Suppose frontier realization tr⁡(Nf)⊆tr⁡(Mf)\operatorname{tr}(N_f)\subseteq\operatorname{tr}(M_f)tr(Nf​)⊆tr(Mf​) holds for every f∈Ff\in Ff∈F. Suppose the upper region has the edge, decomposition, guarded wiring, actual-witness admission, and scope premises of Theorem 1, and roots satisfy their active intents. Under the full closure of these premises,

tr⁡(Nr)⊆UF(r)⊆tr⁡(Mr)⊆Φ(r).\operatorname{tr}(N_r)\subseteq U_F(r)\subseteq\operatorname{tr}(M_r)\subseteq\Phi(r).tr(Nr​)⊆UF​(r)⊆tr(Mr​)⊆Φ(r).

Proof. Simultaneously induct upward on tr⁡(Nv)⊆UF(v)⊆tr⁡(Mv)\operatorname{tr}(N_v)\subseteq U_F(v)\subseteq\operatorname{tr}(M_v)tr(Nv​)⊆UF​(v)⊆tr(Mv​). The frontier case is assumed. Above it, the right inclusion follows from TTT-monotonicity, edge refinement, and decomposition. The left inclusion follows from guarded wiring, whose slot guards follow from the same inductive bounds, and monotonicity into UF(v)U_F(v)UF​(v). Root coverage makes the induction cover every root. □\square□

The root-covering condition ensures that every execution path to a leaf is intercepted by the cut; omitting any branch would discard component behaviors required for parent soundness. Because abstract frontier models provide safe over-approximations of executable behaviors, the theorem yields behavioral containment rather than trace equivalence.

Root coverage guarantees the sound upward transfer of finite-safety trace containment. It does not imply that readiness, unresolved duties, external wait statuses, or human comprehension can be evaluated solely from the cut. Operational progress and interactive inspection require evidence tied directly to the relevant execution witnesses and interfaces.

3.8 Protected boundary inventory

Section titled “3.8 Protected boundary inventory”

Define a tagged disjoint union

Prot⁡(G)=Prot⁡intent(G)⊎Prot⁡slot(G).\operatorname{Prot}(G)=\operatorname{Prot}_{\mathrm{intent}}(G)\uplus\operatorname{Prot}_{\mathrm{slot}}(G).Prot(G)=Protintent​(G)⊎Protslot​(G).

The intent part contains each active root or protected record, including identity, owner, authority, predicate, and scope. The slot part contains every parent-owned record

((v,c),Bv,c,λv,c,Av,c,scopev,c).((v,c),B_{v,c},\lambda_{v,c},A_{v,c},\mathrm{scope}_{v,c}).((v,c),Bv,c​,λv,c​,Av,c​,scopev,c​).

Scope encompasses the formal observation profile, action mapping, declared duty and wait policies (Ed∞E_d^\inftyEd∞​), and environmental context. The protected inventory is a derived projection of accepted intent and slot records, not a duplicate authoring artifact.

Across development steps, governing meaning is preserved by evaluating the evolution condition against the prior protected inventory:

∀p∈Prot⁡(Gt).Preserved⁡(p,Gt+1) ∨ ∃a. AuthorizedDisposition⁡(a,p,Gt+1).(Protect)\forall p\in\operatorname{Prot}(G_t).\quad \operatorname{Preserved}(p,G_{t+1}) \ \lor\ \exists a.\ \operatorname{AuthorizedDisposition}(a,p,G_{t+1}). \tag{Protect}∀p∈Prot(Gt​).Preserved(p,Gt+1​) ∨ ∃a. AuthorizedDisposition(a,p,Gt+1​).(Protect)

Here Preserved⁡(p,Gt+1)\operatorname{Preserved}(p,G_{t+1})Preserved(p,Gt+1​) asserts that the same protected subject and governing meaning remain in force under the same applicable scope; for an active protected intent, this includes continued activation in the support graph. An authorized disposition identifies the prior protected record and records its accepted replacement or intentional retirement under entitled authority. Changes to supporting intents that cause a protected intent to lose activation require an explicit disposition, precisely as direct deletion does.

Authorizations may be granted via standing architectural delegation. Routine implementation adjustments and local refactorings within an authorized grant do not require interactive human re-approval, cryptographic tokens, or third-party signing services. However, modifying a slot contract (such as enlarging a language from {ϵ,ok}\{\epsilon,ok\}{ϵ,ok} to {ϵ,ok,bad}\{\epsilon,ok,bad\}{ϵ,ok,bad}), altering a response duty, or strengthening environmental premises alters protected interface meaning and requires formal architectural re-authorization.

3.9 Human governance and inspectable projections

Section titled “3.9 Human governance and inspectable projections”

Human governance in agent-authored systems operates in two complementary directions: upstream intent authoring and downstream interactive assessment.

During authoring, stakeholders and automated agents must be able to express, inspect, and revise intent from relevant boundary responsibilities, interaction protocols, and operating conditions, without being forced to inspect or reconstruct unrelated implementation code, internal component state machines, or low-level proof scripts. Encapsulated slot contracts and single-owner access boundaries establish the modular units for this authoring reduction.

During assessment, human stakeholders must be able to visually inspect system status, active commitments, component boundaries, recent modifications, evidence strength, unresolved response duties, and external wait prerequisites. Decision-critical context must be exposed directly, while detailed proof transcripts, leaf handler definitions, and full execution traces remain accessible on demand.

A root-covering frontier (§3.7) provides a sound mathematical abstraction for finite-safety inspection, allowing a reviewer to evaluate system safety against high-level component contracts rather than leaf implementations. However, a frontier cut does not by itself establish reduced human cognitive burden:

  • Decision-dependent context: The context required to make a sound governance decision depends on the question being asked. Local questions require narrow views; cross-cutting architectural changes may require global system context. An inspection projection must not create a false impression of local safety by displaying an incomplete, non-covering cut.
  • Inspectable failure: When a failure occurs or a verification check fails, the diagnostic view must identify the affected duty, the reporting boundary, the violated condition, and any remaining uncertainty. It must not manufacture an unverified root-cause attribution.
  • Faithful wait views: A genuine external wait must be displayed accurately as pending at its identified prerequisite (Wd,eW_{d,e}Wd,e​). It must never be presented as a successful completion or an unexplained hang.
  • Assurance status: Any rendered assertion must faithfully reflect the evidential status of the underlying record, distinguishing proved theorems, bounded tests, empirical observations, and refutable hypotheses.

The formal calculus defines these governance requirements and inspection boundaries; it does not mandate a specific UI framework, layout algorithm, or visualization widget, and claims no measured empirical reduction in human effort.

4. Verification Obligations and Restricted Leaf Realization

Section titled “4. Verification Obligations and Restricted Leaf Realization”

4.1 Satisfaction

Section titled “4.1 Satisfaction”

Satisfaction verifies tr⁡(Mv)⊆⟦j⟧\operatorname{tr}(M_v)\subseteq\llbracket j\rrbrackettr(Mv​)⊆[[j]] for each active owned intent. Depending on state complexity, this obligation may be discharged through exhaustive model checking, inductive invariant verification, or sound abstract interpretation. Where finite test suites are employed, universal inclusion requires an accompanying coverage proof demonstrating that all reachable behaviors have been explored.

4.2 Decomposition

Section titled “4.2 Decomposition”

Decomposition establishes Kv((Lv,c)c)⊆tr⁡(Mv)K_v((L_{v,c})_c)\subseteq\operatorname{tr}(M_v)Kv​((Lv,c​)c​)⊆tr(Mv​) strictly against abstract slot contracts rather than concrete child implementations. Consequently, the resulting proof remains valid for any replacement child components that satisfy the same boundary contracts. While the mathematical trajectory definition guarantees monotonicity, the operational fidelity of the composition is established through the guarded wiring obligation.

4.3 Child refinement and deterministic contract monitors

Section titled “4.3 Child refinement and deterministic contract monitors”

A Level-3 monitor is

B=(Q,q0,Σin⊎Σout,β),β:Q×Σvis⇀Q.B=(Q,q_0,\Sigma^{\mathrm{in}}\uplus\Sigma^{\mathrm{out}},\beta),\qquad \beta:Q\times\Sigma^{\mathrm{vis}}\rightharpoonup Q.B=(Q,q0​,Σin⊎Σout,β),β:Q×Σvis⇀Q.

It has one initial state, no hidden transitions, and at most one successor for each state and label. Every reachable state accepts a finite prefix; missing transitions forbid events. Distinct labels such as ok and fail may both be enabled. Determinism does not imply finite state. Every prefix-closed language LLL containing ϵ\epsilonϵ has a canonical such monitor: states are words in LLL, the initial state is ϵ\epsilonϵ, and w→awaw\xrightarrow{a}wawa​wa exactly when wa∈Lwa\in Lwa∈L.

Extend λ\lambdaλ to internal source labels by erasure. An initialized forward simulation R⊆SN×QR\subseteq S_N\times QR⊆SN​×Q relates every source initial state to q0q_0q0​. For every related pair and every source step s→as′s\xrightarrow{a}s'sa​s′, it requires (s′,q)∈R(s',q)\in R(s′,q)∈R when λ(a)=ϵ\lambda(a)=\epsilonλ(a)=ϵ, and otherwise requires β(q,λ(a))=q′\beta(q,\lambda(a))=q'β(q,λ(a))=q′ and (s′,q′)∈R(s',q')\in R(s′,q′)∈R.

Proposition (Simulation Completeness for Deterministic Monitors).

λ∗(tr⁡(N))⊆tr⁡(B)⟺an initialized forward simulation N→B exists.\lambda^*(\operatorname{tr}(N))\subseteq\operatorname{tr}(B) \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \text{an initialized forward simulation }N\to B\text{ exists}.λ∗(tr(N))⊆tr(B)⟺an initialized forward simulation N→B exists.

Proof. A simulation matches each finite run by induction. Conversely, relate sss to every monitor state reached by the mapped trace of a source execution ending in sss. Inclusion admits that trace. Extend its witnessing execution by any source step; determinism makes the monitor state after its old prefix the very state already related to sss, so the new label matches or erases as required. □\square□

This proposition establishes simulation completeness strictly for finite visible-trace inclusion. It does not establish preservation of operational readiness, non-silent response, or divergence freedom. For scoped edge refinement, the simulation equivalence applies directly to the restricted witness Restrict⁡Av,c(N)\operatorname{Restrict}_{A_{v,c}}(N)RestrictAv,c​​(N), while relative input reception and readiness are independently verified on the operational witness (relative reception may share the finite product traversal while remaining a distinct predicate).

The deterministic-target premise is essential. Consider the nondeterministic target with edges 0→a1→b20\xrightarrow{a}1\xrightarrow{b}20a​1b​2 and 0→a2→c30\xrightarrow{a}2\xrightarrow{c}30a​2c​3. Its language is {ϵ,a,ab,ac,abc}\{\epsilon,a,ab,ac,abc\}{ϵ,a,ab,ac,abc}: the shared state 222 also permits ccc after ababab. A source s0→as1s_0\xrightarrow{a}s_1s0​a​s1​, s1→bs2s_1\xrightarrow{b}s_2s1​b​s2​, s1→cs3s_1\xrightarrow{c}s_3s1​c​s3​, s2→cs3s_2\xrightarrow{c}s_3s2​c​s3​ has exactly that language. No simulation exists: after aaa, target state 111 cannot match the source’s ccc, and state 222 cannot match its bbb. Equality of finite trace languages therefore does not suffice for this nondeterministic target.

4.4 Leaf realization and Restricted Leaf Normal Form

Section titled “4.4 Leaf realization and Restricted Leaf Normal Form”

An RLNF leaf is

Dℓ=(Sℓ,s0,ℓ,Iℓ,Oℓ,enℓ,δℓ),D_\ell=(S_\ell,s_{0,\ell},I_\ell,O_\ell,\mathrm{en}_\ell,\delta_\ell),Dℓ​=(Sℓ​,s0,ℓ​,Iℓ​,Oℓ​,enℓ​,δℓ​),

where s0,ℓ∈Sℓs_{0,\ell}\in S_\ells0,ℓ​∈Sℓ​, enℓ:Sℓ→P(Iℓ)\mathrm{en}_\ell:S_\ell\to\mathcal P(I_\ell)enℓ​:Sℓ​→P(Iℓ​), and

δℓ:{(s,i)∣i∈enℓ(s)}⟶Sℓ×List(Oℓ)\delta_\ell:\{(s,i)\mid i\in\mathrm{en}_\ell(s)\}\longrightarrow S_\ell\times\mathrm{List}(O_\ell)δℓ​:{(s,i)∣i∈enℓ​(s)}⟶Sℓ​×List(Oℓ​)

is pure, single-valued, total on its domain, and terminating. All persistent state influencing handler execution is encapsulated within SℓS_\ellSℓ​ or supplied via explicit inputs. Total functional programming primitives, explicit structural recursion, or verified runtime substrates discharge handler termination. Handler termination guarantees that each individual invocation finishes; it does not by itself prove termination of an entire chain of interacting handlers across a connector, nor does it prevent connector-level communication deadlocks.

The microstep elaboration has configurations Sℓ×List(Oℓ)S_\ell\times\mathrm{List}(O_\ell)Sℓ​×List(Oℓ​), initial configuration (s0,ℓ,[])(s_{0,\ell},[])(s0,ℓ​,[]), and exactly two rules:

i∈enℓ(s)δℓ(s,i)=(s′,w)(s,[])→in(i)(s′,w)(s,o::w)→out(o)(s,w).\frac{i\in\mathrm{en}_\ell(s)\quad\delta_\ell(s,i)=(s',w)} {(s,[])\xrightarrow{\mathrm{in}(i)}(s',w)} \qquad \frac{}{(s,o::w)\xrightarrow{\mathrm{out}(o)}(s,w)}.(s,[])in(i)​(s′,w)i∈enℓ​(s)δℓ​(s,i)=(s′,w)​(s,o::w)out(o)​(s,w)​.

No input dispatch occurs while outputs remain in the pending list. The explicit state may already hold the next handler state while the output list records an intermediate observable control point. Pending output lists constitute operational state: a configuration (Done, [ack(i)]) has not yet discharged its root response duty until the output event is emitted. An empty output list is valid whenever the contract owes no immediate response; it does not indicate error, but neither does returning [] excuse an unfulfilled response obligation. Empty lists permit the next enabled input immediately.

For any finite handler chain s0⇒i1/w1s1⋯⇒in/wnsns_0\xRightarrow{i_1/w_1}s_1\cdots\xRightarrow{i_n/w_n}s_ns0​i1​/w1​​s1​⋯in​/wn​​sn​, form the concatenated packets i1w1⋯inwni_1w_1\cdots i_nw_ni1​w1​⋯in​wn​, with input/output tags understood. Let Packets⁡(D)\operatorname{Packets}(D)Packets(D) contain all such words, including ϵ\epsilonϵ.

Lemma (Packet Decomposition).

tr⁡(elab⁡(D))=pref⁡(Packets⁡(D)).\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{elab}(D))=\operatorname{pref}(\operatorname{Packets}(D)).tr(elab(D))=pref(Packets(D)).

Proof. A finite elaborated execution consists of completed packets and possibly a final packet whose output list is only partly drained. Complete that finite list to obtain a packet word extending the trace. Conversely, execute each packet’s input step and output drains; any prefix of that execution is a valid finite execution. The zero-packet and empty-output cases follow from the same rules. □\square□

Substrate operations are externalized:

Iℓ=Ienv⊎Respℓ,Oℓ=Emitℓ⊎Cmdℓ.I_\ell=I_{\mathrm{env}}\uplus\mathrm{Resp}_\ell,\qquad O_\ell=\mathrm{Emit}_\ell\uplus\mathrm{Cmd}_\ell.Iℓ​=Ienv​⊎Respℓ​,Oℓ​=Emitℓ​⊎Cmdℓ​.

A shell Shℓ\mathrm{Sh}_\ellShℓ​ is a formal transition system that receives command outputs and emits corresponding response inputs. The connector specifies synchronization mechanisms, buffering boundaries, response correlations, and outcome domains. The formal shell model captures observable interface interactions, with the physical hardware and substrate fidelity explicitly designated as environmental premises in the trusted base.

The mathematical realization obligation is

tr⁡(elab⁡(Dℓ)) ⁣↾Aℓ⊆tr⁡(Mℓ).\operatorname{tr}(\operatorname{elab}(D_\ell))\!\upharpoonright_{A_\ell} \subseteq\operatorname{tr}(M_\ell).tr(elab(Dℓ​))↾Aℓ​​⊆tr(Mℓ​).

When using host-language implementations PℓP_\ellPℓ​, an explicit translation premise Transℓ\mathrm{Trans}_\ellTransℓ​ formally establishes that the compiled or interpreted runtime witness refines the RLNF microstep elaboration under identical observations, input scopes, and substrate bindings. Composing this translation refinement with the tabular realization proof completely discharges Impl⁡\operatorname{Impl}Impl for finite visible-trace safety.

Operational properties—relative reception, readiness, and non-silent response—require evidence about the actual runtime execution witness or an explicit correspondence preserving those properties. Trace containment alone cannot establish them. When the mathematical elaboration is itself the executable artifact, identity supplies this correspondence. Running the elaboration through a host runtime or interpreter introduces a runtime boundary; that boundary must be justified by its execution semantics rather than assumed identical by naming the source table. The single Impl⁡\operatorname{Impl}Impl obligation encompasses this realization chain, maintaining distinguishable evidence scopes without requiring artificial API splits.

Here inputs denote dispatch. An asynchronous arrival buffer, if used, has separate enqueue and dispatch transitions; dispatch removes its head only when the leaf is ready and that input is enabled. Pending output drains never remove buffered inputs. Such a buffer is an owned component or substrate primitive requiring its own conformance evidence. The synchronous connector in §8 needs no mailbox. In either case, an empty output list in AwaitFsync enables only its declared completion inputs, not a new ordinary request.

4.4.1 Verifying readiness and complete-execution duties

Section titled “4.4.1 Verifying readiness and complete-execution duties”

Verifying the operational obligations of §2.5 requires techniques tailored to execution witnesses rather than language containment:

  • Readiness (Ready\mathrm{Ready}Ready): For finite-state systems, readiness is verified by reachable-configuration exploration. At each reachable configuration (s,h)(s,h)(s,h), the checker confirms that either an external wait Wd,eW_{d,e}Wd,e​ holds or at least one owned continuation step s→owned(d)s′s \xrightarrow{\mathrm{owned}(d)} s'sowned(d)​s′ is enabled. For synchronous connectors, the check evaluates composite states to confirm that the recipient is receptive to the proposed step.
  • Non-silent response (NS\mathrm{NS}NS): Verifying NS\mathrm{NS}NS requires analyzing complete maximal executions in CExec⁡v(Nv,ω)\operatorname{CExec}_v(N_v,\omega)CExecv​(Nv​,ω). A reachable terminal or quiescent configuration where duty ddd is outstanding without an active genuine external wait constitutes an immediate counterexample. For infinite executions, finite-state cycle detection over the synchronized product evaluates whether any reachable cycle contains outstanding duties without emitting a permitted outcome or persistently remaining in a permitted wait (e∈Ed∞e \in E_d^\inftye∈Ed∞​). Any such cycle must be shown unreachable, or shown to be excluded by an explicit, warranted scheduling or fairness premise.
  • Deductive ranking: For systems with infinite state spaces or complex control loops, developers may supply a well-founded ranking function or variant that strictly decreases across owned continuation steps toward outcome emission or wait entry.

The calculus does not mandate syntactically acyclic code, automatic ranking synthesis, universal strong fairness, or artificial watchdog timers. A loop with cyclic control syntax is fully admissible provided its execution terminates or satisfies the required response condition. The evidence record simply documents the verification method, its completeness, its assumptions, and the runtime conditions under which progress is assured.

4.5 Evidence discipline

Section titled “4.5 Evidence discipline”

An evidence record explicitly documents the obligation, target claim, verification method, execution outcome, underlying assumptions, architectural scope, and verified artifact. Different verification approaches—deductive model proofs, exhaustive finite exploration, bounded analysis, runtime conformance observations, and empirical human-task evaluations—provide distinct formal assurances and must remain strictly separated. Missing or incomplete evidence leaves an obligation unresolved; while an empty result may be valid for a generic query, the absence of a required subject cannot be reported as coverage of that subject. Following the foundational principles of the Evidential Tool Bus (Rushby, 2005; Cruanes et al., 2013, 2014) and Assurance 2.0 (Bloomfield, Netkachova, and Rushby, 2024), verification results are maintained as structured, typed arguments, ensuring that tool evidence directly matches the strength and assumptions of its claimed obligation.

4.6 Three-gate structure

Section titled “4.6 Three-gate structure”

The evidence gate evaluates three orthogonal dimensions of acceptance: behavioral validity, confirming mathematical trace inclusions and committed operational/temporal duties; authority preservation, verifying that protected intents and slot contracts conform to architectural authorizations; and evidence applicability, confirming that proof artifacts, environmental scopes, and candidate binaries match the target obligation precisely.

4.7 Consolidated trusted base

Section titled “4.7 Consolidated trusted base”

The following inventory collects the premises that connect the mathematical argument to an implementation. Items proved in a particular deployment cease to be assumptions there, but their boundary obligations do not disappear.

Boundary Required evidence or explicit premise What is not inferred
Intent and context interpretation Accepted predicates, authority, scopes, feasible environment interpretation That a formalized requirement matches every unstated user expectation
Mathematical proof / checker Sound inference and applicable checker semantics or checked certificates Universal validity from a bare process exit code
RLNF handlers Totality, purity, explicit-state closure, enabled-input definition Termination from syntax alone or state-freedom from an empty object
Source-to-RLNF translation Transℓ\mathrm{Trans}_\ellTransℓ​ specifying exact code, runtime, and preserved properties Correctness of arbitrary host-language code or runtime progress from trace safety
Runtime and connector Adm⁡\operatorname{Adm}Adm, ownership, relative reception, guarded Wire⁡\operatorname{Wire}Wire, scope erasure, and scheduling/execution semantics for progress Legal delivery or progress from local trace inclusion alone
Physical substrate Command/response meaning, failure model, durability hypothesis, and conditional external-response premises (including HwriteH_{\mathrm{write}}Hwrite​) Physical persistence or eventual response from symbolic labels or shell graphs alone
Evolution and evidence storage Operand identity or proved transport; coherent candidate publication and preserved audit records Semantic equivalence from labels, paths, or cryptographic hashes alone
Human reading and inspection Faithful decision-relevant projections and appropriately scoped evaluation tasks Cognitive context reduction or governance correctness from graph proofs or visualizations alone

5. Decomposition, Modularity, and Interaction

Section titled “5. Decomposition, Modularity, and Interaction”

5.1 Contracts are relational

Section titled “5.1 Contracts are relational”

Proposition 1 (Coordinate Projections Erase Correlation). A relation need not equal the product of its coordinate projections.

Proof. For R={(0,0),(1,1)}R=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}R={(0,0),(1,1)}, both projections are {0,1}\{0,1\}{0,1}. Their product also contains (0,1)(0,1)(0,1) and (1,0)(1,0)(1,0), which are not in RRR. □\square□

Accordingly, independent child predicates do not establish an interaction property such as matching transaction identifiers or coherent shared-state updates. The owning connector’s joint trajectories retain that correlation. Decomposition verifies the property where the interaction is owned.

5.2 Sibling independence and safety substitution

Section titled “5.2 Sibling independence and safety substitution”

Theorem 2 (Safety Substitution). Fix a parent’s context, admission domain, contracts, abstractions, input scopes, and connector. If replacement witnesses are admissible and satisfy every fixed slot, the same guarded wiring and decomposition proofs establish their composite inclusion in tr⁡(Mv)\operatorname{tr}(M_v)tr(Mv​). An unchanged sibling needs no new local refinement proof solely because another child was replaced.

Proof. Instantiate the existing universal wiring certificate with the replacement tuple. Slot conformance gives its guard. Monotonicity and the fixed decomposition yield the inclusion, exactly as in Theorem 1. □\square□

Theorem 2 establishes formal proof modularity for finite visible-trace safety: verifying a localized component replacement preserves parent safety whenever external slot contracts are respected.

This locality principle applies to other behavioral properties only when accompanied by an applicable composition or transport argument. In particular, Theorem 2 does not establish compositional progress or non-silent response. Mutually dependent progress obligations can form circular dependencies: component A waits for an event from B, while B waits for an event from A. Both local conditional progress obligations may hold vacuously while the composite system deadlocks. A parent response commitment must verify composite execution explicitly to ensure that circular waiting is absent.

5.3 Executable closure

Section titled “5.3 Executable closure”

Every executable behavior contributing to a root system is explicitly owned by an RLNF leaf, a declared connector transition, or a declared substrate primitive. Architectural routing skeletons synchronize and map events, while persistent queues, transaction managers, and shared scheduling mechanisms are represented as explicit owned components or declared runtime/substrate state, with the applicable proof or hypothesis retained in the dependency closure.

5.4 Single-owner shared services via parent-connector serialization

Section titled “5.4 Single-owner shared services via parent-connector serialization”

A parent component may own a stateful service and mediate requests originating from multiple client branches. A serializing connector coordinates client access by granting service access to at most one outstanding operation at a time, recording client identities, and delivering responses back to the originating client. The shared state is owned explicitly by a coordinator or verified runtime primitive.

The serializing connector chosen here orders service invocations. The shared-counter example illustrates its aggregate contract; shared mutable state alone does not impose this particular serialization strategy. Interleaved or pipelined access can be supported by adopting alternative connector semantics, such as linearizable concurrent data structures (Herlihy and Wing, 1990; Filipović et al., 2010), provided the resulting joint trajectories are verified against the parent contract.

5.5 Verified and substrate libraries

Section titled “5.5 Verified and substrate libraries”

Verified third-party libraries integrate into the development DAG through declared interfaces, applicable refinement evidence, and clear runtime ownership bindings. Components that fall outside RLNF are modeled as declared substrate boundaries supported by an explicit hypothesis or a separately established translation or refinement result. In accordance with compositional design, specifications adopt the minimal contract strength necessary to establish parent requirements; any relied-on progress promise requires its own applicable argument.

5.6 Admissible-input databases

Section titled “5.6 Admissible-input databases”

General storage interfaces frequently support rich query protocols, whereas an application may rely upon a disciplined transaction sequence. By formalizing this usage pattern as an input scope AAA and proving that the owning connector delivers only admissible sequences, component refinement is established on the relevant operating domain, provided that required operating uses are not excluded from AAA merely to pass a check. Durability guarantees, transaction isolation levels, and failure models are formalized as explicit boundary premises, ensuring that transactional semantics remain verified relative to those premises.

6. The Development Protocol

Section titled “6. The Development Protocol”

6.1 Five development gates

Section titled “6.1 Five development gates”

The development protocol organizes verification into five gates, distinct from the three evidence dimensions in §4.6.

Gate Required result
G1: Declare Fix accepted intents, scopes, authority, response duties, permitted failure conditions, external wait policies (Ed∞E_d^\inftyEd∞​), and the contract-inclusive Prot⁡(G)\operatorname{Prot}(G)Prot(G). Separate open questions and hypotheses from commitments.
G2: Model Establish typed machines, contexts, input protocols, ownership, and satisfaction obligations without deactivating failed intents.
G3: Decompose Fix parent slots and connector semantics; prove decomposition and guarded wiring for the stated witness domain.
G4: Realize Prove child refinements, RLNF realizations, operational readiness, translation premises where needed, and actual-witness admission.
G5: Integrate Check the full dependency closure, all applicable evidence, operational non-silent response, protected dispositions, and the integrated candidate before publication.

These gates structure development responsibilities and evaluation criteria. They do not mandate a serialized, multi-pass tool pipeline; a unified analysis engine may check multiple gates during a single traversal. Publication requires that all five gates pass; an unresolved operational duty cannot be published merely because finite-safety checks succeeded.

6.2 Authoring cycle and discriminating regressions

Section titled “6.2 Authoring cycle and discriminating regressions”

When introducing a modification, developers identify the target requirement and its owning architectural boundary. Target specifications and discriminating test cases are established prior to implementation. Discriminating cases must explicitly cover critical failure modes: silent duty loss, enabled-but-untaken continuations, genuine external waiting, resolved-but-undrained pending outputs, and composite mutual waiting. Expected rejections are determined by the formal specification, never copied from candidate tool output. Complete verification records, counterexamples, and regression suites are retained across iterations to support rigorous evaluation.

6.3 Authority and repair

Section titled “6.3 Authority and repair”

An implementation author may modify internal component behavior while preserving incoming slot contracts. A slot revision, an intent revision, and an environmental assumption change are distinct architectural actions requiring separate authorization. Editing a test to match an implementation does not establish the original requirement.

When an implementation defect is identified, it is repaired directly within the existing component boundary. Governing revisions may proceed under an applicable standing delegation; notification of proof success does not by itself constitute authorization. Routine engineering decisions are resolved within authorized grants. Accepted informal or unresolved intent remains governing: if a material conflict or ambiguity arises in accepted system requirements, only the affected action is paused and escalated for an explicit architectural decision, while independent authorized work continues; until every accepted commitment governing a target scope is formalized into Prot⁡(G)\operatorname{Prot}(G)Prot(G) and discharged (or explicitly disposed by an authorized decision), publication of that scope remains Unresolved. Once a protected revision is authorized, all resulting validity obligations still apply.

7. Versioned Evolution and Incremental Frame Cutoff

Section titled “7. Versioned Evolution and Incremental Frame Cutoff”

7.1 Versioned developments

Section titled “7.1 Versioned developments”

A version sequence (Gt)t(G_t)_t(Gt​)t​ retains prior records and evidence. A candidate Gt+1G_{t+1}Gt+1​ is distinct from a verified published version. Let Req⁡(G)\operatorname{Req}(G)Req(G) be its set of typed scoped obligations, including all finite-safety inclusions, relative reception, operational readiness, and contract-relative non-silent response duties. Publication checks the protected inventory via condition (Protect)(\mathrm{Protect})(Protect) on prior protected subjects (§3.8), alongside all structural, admission, context, and integration premises; merely discharging changed formulas is insufficient.

An authorized disposition records the original protected subject, its accepted updated specification or retirement, the governing authority, and the applicable scope. Across each published version, logical cells resolve to coherent definitions, with distinct stateful runtime instances maintaining unique runtime identities.

7.2 Contextual projection and staleness

Section titled “7.2 Contextual projection and staleness”

When an accepted intent motivates a stronger child contract or an alternative decomposition, the proposed structure is validated by re-establishing parent decomposition and context entailments. Modifications propagate along semantic dependency paths: downstream obligations remain pending until prior evidence is demonstrated to be applicable (by exact operand identity or a justified transport argument) or fresh proofs are supplied. A modification requires examining affected applicability rather than automatically reproving unaffected subgraphs.

7.4 Corollary 2: Interface cutoff

Section titled “7.4 Corollary 2: Interface cutoff”

Corollary 2 (Interface Cutoff). Replace a region while fixing all external boundary operands: slot contracts, maps, input scopes, parent model and intents, connector and admission domain, runtime interpretation, and contexts. Once the replacement’s local and incoming refinement obligations are established, the parent Wire⁡\operatorname{Wire}Wire and Dec⁡\operatorname{Dec}Dec proofs are reusable, as are other operand-identical obligations with applicable evidence.

Proof. Universal wiring does not contain a particular child’s implementation as an operand. The fixed parent decomposition contains slot languages rather than child models. Their typed propositions are unchanged; apply Theorem 3. □\square□

A leaf-code change with fixed MℓM_\ellMℓ​ changes realization but not incoming model refinement. A child-model change can change incoming refinement without changing the fixed parent slot. A split or merge changes the direct parent’s slot signature and wiring, so cutoff occurs above the first preserved boundary, not at the modified connector itself. Changing a slot guard, input scope, substrate meaning, or runtime interpretation is not an unchanged-boundary case.

Reusing operational readiness or progress arguments similarly requires verifying that underlying execution dependencies and scheduling premises remain preserved or justified by an applicable transport argument. An unchanged safety slot alone is insufficient; conversely, a localized, progress-preserving leaf modification does not invalidate unrelated sibling components. Universal parent proof reuse is also distinct from caching implementation-sensitive diagnostics, which depend on concrete child realizations rather than abstract slot contracts alone.

This result provides an obligation-level instance of early cutoff: re-verification of unaffected subgraphs terminates as soon as external interface operands are confirmed unchanged, adapting the dependency-tracking principles of modern build systems (Mokhov, Mitchell, and Peyton Jones, 2018) to formal verification obligations.

7.5 Typed evolution and four-way failure diagnosis

Section titled “7.5 Typed evolution and four-way failure diagnosis”

Define the tagged outcome type

EvolutionResult=Verified(Development,Evidence,AuthorizedDispositions)∣Conflict(Development,ConflictWitness)∣Unresolved(Development,Pfin(Obligation)).\begin{aligned} \mathrm{EvolutionResult}={}& \mathrm{Verified}(\mathrm{Development},\mathrm{Evidence},\mathrm{AuthorizedDispositions})\\ &\mid\mathrm{Conflict}(\mathrm{Development},\mathrm{ConflictWitness})\\ &\mid\mathrm{Unresolved}(\mathrm{Development},\mathcal P_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathrm{Obligation})). \end{aligned}EvolutionResult=​Verified(Development,Evidence,AuthorizedDispositions)∣Conflict(Development,ConflictWitness)∣Unresolved(Development,Pfin​(Obligation)).​

An evolution procedure has the partial-function type

evolve⁡:Development×AuthorizedDelta⇀EvolutionResult.\operatorname{evolve}:\mathrm{Development}\times\mathrm{AuthorizedDelta} \rightharpoonup\mathrm{EvolutionResult}.evolve:Development×AuthorizedDelta⇀EvolutionResult.

The payload types represent the possible outcomes of development evolution: Verified denotes a candidate that satisfies all publication and verification gates across the entire selected profile (including committed operational duties, not safety alone); Conflict documents a demonstrated incompatibility among accepted requirements or environmental premises; and Unresolved captures open proof obligations and pending implementation adjustments requiring further automated or human intervention. A pending external request at runtime is an operational execution status, not one of these verification-outcome constructors.

After applying an authorized delta, recompute active intents, exact obligations, dependency closure, and protected dispositions. Check premise compatibility and evidence applicability. A failed attempt is classified into four evidentially distinct cases:

  1. Concrete violation: a legal joint executable run violates the accepted predicate. Repair the implementation or owning integration boundary.
  2. Abstract counterexample: a model or contract trajectory violates its target, but runtime feasibility is not established. Refine the offending abstraction or produce a concrete witness before calling it a runtime bug.
  3. Failed proof witness: a proposed invariant or simulation does not close. Repair the proof witness or investigate further; this does not itself refute inclusion.
  4. Unknown: timeout, unsupported reasoning, or missing evidence. Preserve the open obligation without classifying it as true, false, genuine, or spurious.

This taxonomy synthesizes counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (Clarke et al., 2003) with the eliminative argumentation of Assurance 2.0 (Bloomfield, Netkachova, and Rushby, 2024), clearly distinguishing concrete runtime bugs, spurious abstraction artifacts, and solver incompleteness.

7.6 Joint trajectory feasibility and repair direction

Section titled “7.6 Joint trajectory feasibility and repair direction”

For an abstract parent counterexample τ\tauτ, model-level feasibility is

∃r. legal⁡Wv(r)∧obs⁡v(r)=τ∧∀c, slice⁡c(r)∈Tv,c(tr⁡(Mc)).\exists r.\ \operatorname{legal}_{W_v}(r)\land\operatorname{obs}_v(r)=\tau \land\forall c,\ \operatorname{slice}_c(r)\in T_{v,c}(\operatorname{tr}(M_c)).∃r. legalWv​​(r)∧obsv​(r)=τ∧∀c, slicec​(r)∈Tv,c​(tr(Mc​)).

Proposition 2 (Joint Trajectory Feasibility). The displayed condition is equivalent to τ∈Kv((Tv,c(tr⁡(Mc)))c)\tau\in K_v((T_{v,c}(\operatorname{tr}(M_c)))_c)τ∈Kv​((Tv,c​(tr(Mc​)))c​). Separate per-child existential witnesses do not imply it.

Proof. The equivalence is the definition of KvK_vKv​. For the second claim, let one shared trajectory bit bbb be fixed. One child requires b=0b=0b=0 and another requires b=1b=1b=1. Each has a separate witness; no single trajectory has both values. □\square□

Establishing the runtime feasibility of an abstract counterexample requires exhibiting a concrete joint execution witness or providing an applicable realization or completeness argument for that trajectory. A forward simulation over-approximation alone is insufficient. Proving a two-way simulation completeness theorem between model and implementation is one sufficient method, but is not mandatory if a direct execution witness is demonstrated.

Identifying the appropriate repair direction depends on whether the defect resides in component implementation or architectural abstraction. For example, if a child component correctly produces {ϵ,ok}\{\epsilon,ok\}{ϵ,ok} while its abstraction over-approximates behaviors with {ϵ,ok,bad}\{\epsilon,ok,bad\}{ϵ,ok,bad}, the appropriate repair refines the child abstraction rather than altering the parent slot. Conversely, if a decomposition fails because parent slots permit invalid interleavings, strengthening the slot contracts resolves the issue, provided child components can fulfill the tighter requirements and the contract change is formally authorized. Publish only after all gates pass; otherwise retain the candidate, evidence, and open obligations.

8. End-to-End Worked Example: Durable Acknowledgement

8.1 Requirement and scope

Section titled “8.1 Requirement and scope”

One runtime instance handles at most one request carrying identifier i∈Idi\in\mathrm{Id}i∈Id. The visible root requirement is: ack(i) is preceded by the matching commit_ok(i); a failure branch emits commit_fail(i) and fail(i) instead. A named substrate hypothesis HdurH_{\mathrm{dur}}Hdur​ states that a matching successful flush response after the modeled write establishes durability under the declared storage/crash model. It is a forward implication, not an assertion that every durable write must return success.

The environment supplies at most one request. In this modeled scope, file writing produces a successful write_ok response, while flush may succeed, fail, or remain pending. Acceptance of req(i) opens a root response duty ddd, discharged only when root ack(i) or permitted root fail(i) is emitted. Failure is contractually tied to the modeled unsuccessful flush branch.

In the operational model, the modeled successful write guarantee is formalized as an explicit premise HwriteH_{\mathrm{write}}Hwrite​: following a synchronized Cmd.write(i), the matching response write_ok(i) eventually occurs. Consequently, write waiting is strictly transient. In contrast, an unresolved flush operation may remain pending indefinitely as a genuine, inspectable external wait (Ed∞={flush(i)}E_d^\infty = \{\mathrm{flush}(i)\}Ed∞​={flush(i)}); the system does not invent a timeout, fabricate an unobserved failure, or assume eventual flush completion. Finite-safety verification does not require HwriteH_{\mathrm{write}}Hwrite​; the scoped progress argument uses it explicitly.

Use these same scopes for the leaf realization obligations. They exclude wrong identifiers, duplicates, contradictory outcomes, and spontaneous response inputs. They do not express that a response follows a command output or that committed follows coordinator append; those causal facts require the connector and slot guarantees.

C0C_0C0​ is a synchronous product of the two child witnesses and the shell of §8.5, with the following rules. A coordinator append(i) output synchronizes with the store’s append(i) input. Store committed(i) and failed(i) outputs synchronize with the matching coordinator inputs. Each store command synchronizes with the shell’s command input; each shell response synchronizes with the store’s corresponding input. Unshared child events interleave. Child internal events interleave and are hidden. The environment supplies only the permitted root request. Shared events occur only when both participants have the transition; no event is fabricated or duplicated.

There is no arrival queue in this connector. Reception is checked at the paired states before each synchronous delivery. A deployment adding buffering must establish its distinct arrival/dispatch refinement (§4.4).

W0W_0W0​ is the same finite-trajectory synchronization scheme over slot words and shell paths. Its root observation keeps coordinator req, ack, and fail, maps store flush_ok to commit_ok and flush_fail to commit_fail, and erases every other event. This is again a letter-or-erasure projection. Each root trajectory retains both component slices, including hidden commands, responses, and routed events, so it does not discard their causal correlation.
