8.6 Causal delivery, wiring, decomposition, and root soundness

Section titled “8.6 Causal delivery, wiring, decomposition, and root soundness”

We prove guarded Wire⁡(0)\operatorname{Wire}(0)Wire(0) for arbitrary admissible witnesses refining the two fixed slots, not just the tables. The shell and synchronization rules are fixed operands. Consider a supposed first delivery outside a declared input scope. Before it, every child input history is in scope, so its executed prefix and any output extending that prefix are governed by its slot inclusion: outputs cannot be hidden by the input restriction.

The external request is single-use and matching by the root environment premise. A coordinator append(i) can occur only after that req(i), once. The store can issue Cmd.write(i) only after receiving append(i); the shell can return write_ok(i) only after receiving that command. A store Cmd.fsync(i) can occur only after the matching write response, and the shell can supply at most one matching flush outcome. Finally, a store committed(i) or failed(i) can occur only after its matching flush event, itself after append(i). Thus coordinator response delivery is after its append output has drained and is single-use, matching, and non-spontaneous.

To make the first-invalid-input argument fully explicit, suppose for contradiction that some composite step delivers a first input prefix violating either A0,coordA_{0,\mathrm{coord}}A0,coord​ or A0,storeA_{0,\mathrm{store}}A0,store​:

  1. First invalid input delivered to the coordinator: The only permitted inputs in A0,coordA_{0,\mathrm{coord}}A0,coord​ are an initial single req(i)\mathrm{req}(i)req(i), followed by at most one matching committed(i)\mathrm{committed}(i)committed(i) or failed(i)\mathrm{failed}(i)failed(i). A violation would require: (a) a spurious or duplicate req(j)\mathrm{req}(j)req(j), which is barred by the root environment premise; (b) a spontaneous committed(i)\mathrm{committed}(i)committed(i) or failed(i)\mathrm{failed}(i)failed(i) prior to emitting append(i)\mathrm{append}(i)append(i), which contradicts the store slot B0,storeB_{0,\mathrm{store}}B0,store​ (which requires append(i)\mathrm{append}(i)append(i) before any response); or (c) an outcome with mismatched identifier j≠ij \ne ij=i or a contradictory second outcome, both barred by the single-identifier execution of B0,storeB_{0,\mathrm{store}}B0,store​ and shell synchronization.
  2. First invalid input delivered to the store: Under the fixed shell Shstore\mathrm{Sh}_{\mathrm{store}}Shstore​ and command synchronization, admissible delivered input histories to the store consist of an initial append(i)\mathrm{append}(i)append(i), followed by write_ok(i)\mathrm{write\_ok}(i)write_ok(i) strictly after Cmd.write(i)\mathrm{Cmd.write}(i)Cmd.write(i), and finally fsync_ok(i)\mathrm{fsync\_ok}(i)fsync_ok(i) or fsync_fail(i)\mathrm{fsync\_fail}(i)fsync_fail(i) strictly after Cmd.fsync(i)\mathrm{Cmd.fsync}(i)Cmd.fsync(i). A violation would require: (a) a spurious or duplicate append(j)\mathrm{append}(j)append(j), which contradicts coordinator slot conformance (the coordinator emits append(i)\mathrm{append}(i)append(i) at most once, strictly in response to req(i)\mathrm{req}(i)req(i)); or (b) an unsolicited, out-of-order, or duplicate shell response, which contradicts the transition structure of Shstore\mathrm{Sh}_{\mathrm{store}}Shstore​ (which transitions to response states only upon receiving the corresponding command from the store).

Every branch of this finite case split contradicts the causal prefixes of the component slots and shell. All delivered histories therefore lie in the stated AAA sets, including the intrinsic leaf scopes.

This argument also checks readiness: the routed append reaches the store’s initial input state; each shell response reaches the corresponding store input state; and the store result reaches coordinator c2(i)c_2(i)c2​(i), not its pending-append state. Relative reception of the admitted witnesses supplies the matching input transition. Hidden internal source steps cannot change the deterministic monitor state. Thus the proof does not rely on suppressing an invalid delivery by composing already restricted machines. If a raw witness had a first bad delivery, the same prefix argument would exclude it.

For routing adequacy, induct on concrete composite steps. An unshared transition extends one component slice; a synchronization extends both participating slices with the shared event; a shell step also extends the shell path. The retained joint record is legal for W0W_0W0​ and has exactly the root observation defined in §8.3. Combining this slicing invariant with the proved input scopes gives Delivery⁡0\operatorname{Delivery}_0Delivery0​ and the restricted inclusion required by Wire⁡(0)\operatorname{Wire}(0)Wire(0).

For Dec⁡(0)\operatorname{Dec}(0)Dec(0), take any legal trajectory whose slices belong to the slot languages. If no root request has occurred, its root observation is empty. After req(i), the coordinator emits append(i) at most once. The store’s selected branch can contribute either commit_ok(i) followed eventually, if the trajectory continues, by coordinator ack(i), or commit_fail(i) followed by fail(i). The coordinator cannot acknowledge before receiving the store result, which follows the matching flush event. No other root events are possible. Hence every root observation is in L0L_0L0​, including truncations at all hidden or visible intermediate events.

The two edge refinements are immediate because restriction selects a sublanguage (tr⁡(Mc) ⁣↾A0,c⊆tr⁡(Mc)\operatorname{tr}(M_c)\!\upharpoonright_{A_{0,c}} \subseteq \operatorname{tr}(M_c)tr(Mc​)↾A0,c​​⊆tr(Mc​)), the edge maps λ0,c\lambda_{0,c}λ0,c​ are identities, and the local component machines are defined by Mc=B0,cM_c=B_{0,c}Mc​=B0,c​. The simulations establish realization; the delivery proof justifies the shared input scopes; the product has a nonempty initial state and accepts the permitted initial request. Root satisfaction is tr⁡(M0)=L0⊆Φ0\operatorname{tr}(M_0)=L_0\subseteq\Phi_0tr(M0​)=L0​⊆Φ0​, where Φ0\Phi_0Φ0​ is a necessary safety predicate requiring that every ack(i) be preceded by commit_ok(i) and every fail(i) by commit_fail(i) (with request precedence and branch mutual exclusivity ensured by L0L_0L0​). Theorem 1 therefore yields the complete root trace inclusion. Under hypothesis HdurH_{\mathrm{dur}}Hdur​, emitting ack(i) establishes that the successful write has been durably flushed to persistent storage, with the overall root guarantee formally supported by the combined environment, shell, and runtime premises in H0H_0H0​.

A spontaneous-output store serves as an informative negative witness: even if receptive and properly initialized, emitting an initial committed(i) violates its slot contract and is decisively rejected by the universal wiring guard.

8.6.1 Readiness, non-silent progress, and external wait

We evaluate operational readiness and non-silent response on the synchronized composite execution witness N0=C0[Ncoord,Nstore,Shstore]N_0 = C_0[N_{\mathrm{coord}}, N_{\mathrm{store}}, \mathrm{Sh}_{\mathrm{store}}]N0​=C0​[Ncoord​,Nstore​,Shstore​].

  • Pending duty (PdP_dPd​): Duty ddd is pending in all composite states following external input req(i) prior to the emission of root ack(i) or fail(i).
  • Transient write wait (Wd,write(i)W_{d,\mathrm{write}(i)}Wd,write(i)​): A genuine write wait is the composite configuration with coordinator (Await(i), []), store (AwaitWrite(i), []), and shell hW(i)hW(i)hW(i) following the synchronized Cmd.write(i). Here Wd,write(i)W_{d,\mathrm{write}(i)}Wd,write(i)​ holds because the system awaits the external write response. Under premise HwriteH_{\mathrm{write}}Hwrite​, this wait is transient; it is excluded from persistent waiting (Ed∞E_d^\inftyEd∞​).
  • Genuine persistent flush wait (Wd,flush(i)W_{d,\mathrm{flush}(i)}Wd,flush(i)​): A genuine flush wait is the composite configuration with coordinator (Await(i), []), store (AwaitFsync(i), []), and shell hPending(i)hPending(i)hPending(i) following Cmd.fsync(i). The root contract explicitly permits this wait to persist indefinitely:
Ed∞={the matching flush prerequisite flush(i)}.E_d^\infty = \{\text{the matching flush prerequisite } \mathrm{flush}(i)\}.Ed∞​={the matching flush prerequisite flush(i)}.
  • Owned continuations: Configurations with pending outputs—such as store (Done, [flush_ok(i), committed(i)]), store (Done, [committed(i)]), or coordinator (Done, [ack(i)])—are not external waits. They represent owned internal work that must be drained.
  • Inspection exposure: Correlated composite wait states are exposed through the inspection projection, identifying the outstanding duty and prerequisite. They indicate pending status, not durable completion or failure.

The composite transition system over the single request is acyclic: every owned handler execution and output drain advances along a finite directed acyclic graph. At every pending configuration where neither Wd,write(i)W_{d,\mathrm{write}(i)}Wd,write(i)​ nor Wd,flush(i)W_{d,\mathrm{flush}(i)}Wd,flush(i)​ holds, an owned continuation transition is enabled: coordinator pending outputs (append(i), ack(i), fail(i)) synchronize with the receptive initial store or emit externally; store pending outputs (Cmd.write(i), Cmd.fsync(i), flush_ok(i), committed(i), etc.) synchronize with the receptive shell or coordinator; and once outputs drain after a shell response (write_ok(i), fsync_ok(i), or fsync_fail(i)), the corresponding store handler is enabled by proved relative reception. Execution Premise Hexec0H_{\mathrm{exec}}^0Hexec0​: For every boundary-owned transition on the example’s finite per-request continuation, if that transition remains continuously enabled while duty ddd is outstanding, it is not postponed forever.

Premise Hexec0H_{\mathrm{exec}}^0Hexec0​ is a per-transition weak-fairness condition over the finite continuation of this specific example. It is not a general theorem about host schedulers, nor does it assert universal progress for cyclic systems.

8.7 Premature-commit regression and non-progress regressions

Section titled “8.7 Premature-commit regression and non-progress regressions”

To demonstrate the discriminating power of the calculus, we evaluate candidate mutant implementations against the established safety and operational obligations.

8.7.1 Premature-acknowledgement safety regression

Section titled “8.7.1 Premature-acknowledgement safety regression”

Consider a faulty store handler Idle + append(i) -> Done, [committed(i)], with the other initial inputs unchanged. Its trace append(i), committed(i) is rejected by the fixed store graph: after append(i) the next required visible output is Cmd.write(i), and the projected public protocol also requires flush_ok(i) before committed(i). The input history [append(i)] is admissible, so input restriction does not remove the counterexample.

Composed with the coordinator, this witness produces the root trace req(i), ack(i). It is not in L0L_0L0​, because ack(i) lacks its preceding commit_ok(i). The expected rejection is stated by the unchanged graphs, not copied from the faulty implementation. This run does not contradict Theorem 1: the faulty store fails realization/refinement, so the universal wiring guard cannot be instantiated for it.

8.7.2 Operational non-progress regressions

Section titled “8.7.2 Operational non-progress regressions”

The following structural scenarios illustrate how operational obligations (Ready)(\mathrm{Ready})(Ready) and (NS)(\mathrm{NS})(NS) reject invalid behaviors that satisfy finite-safety trace containment:

  1. Silent terminal loss: Replace the coordinator request handler by Idle + req(i) -> Done, []. The finite trace language {ϵ,req(i)}\{\epsilon, \mathrm{req}(i)\}{ϵ,req(i)} satisfies safety inclusion, but the response duty is abandoned. The completed configuration has PdP_dPd​, no DdD_dDd​, no WWW, and no enabled owned transition. It is decisively rejected by Ready\mathrm{Ready}Ready and NS\mathrm{NS}NS.
  2. Enabled-but-untaken outcome loop: Consider an operational witness whose runtime admits an internal self-loop while a terminal outcome transition remains continuously enabled. This execution satisfies finite trace inclusion and condition (Ready)(\mathrm{Ready})(Ready), but fails (NS)(\mathrm{NS})(NS) because the duty is never discharged. Premise Hexec0H_{\mathrm{exec}}^0Hexec0​ excludes this behavior for the acyclic example, but a general runtime lacking fairness must treat this regression as a real failure mode.
  3. Resolved-but-undrained output: Following fsync_ok(i), the store transitions to Done with pending list [flush_ok(i), committed(i)]. If the runtime halts output draining, the prerequisite has resolved, so Wd,flush(i)W_{d,\mathrm{flush}(i)}Wd,flush(i)​ ceases to hold. The execution stalls with an outstanding duty and no wait explanation, violating NS\mathrm{NS}NS.
  4. Persistent flush wait accepted: A complete execution that issues Cmd.fsync(i) and remains permanently in hPending(i)hPending(i)hPending(i) satisfies NS\mathrm{NS}NS via its second disjunct, because flush(i)∈Ed∞\mathrm{flush}(i) \in E_d^\inftyflush(i)∈Ed∞​. The system correctly reports the duty as pending without manufacturing an artificial timeout or error.
  5. Parent-owned mutual waiting: Suppose two internal child components deadlock waiting for each other. Because both components lie within the parent boundary’s realization, their mutual dependency is internal work. The parent cannot classify this internal blockage as an external wait (Wd,eW_{d,e}Wd,e​). The complete stalled execution fails Ready\mathrm{Ready}Ready and NS\mathrm{NS}NS.
  6. Strict contract with persistent wait: Consider a strict terminal-response contract with Ed∞=∅E_d^\infty = \emptysetEd∞​=∅. A complete execution that stalls permanently in hPending(i)hPending(i)hPending(i) fails NS\mathrm{NS}NS, whereas an execution with a transient wait followed by terminal acknowledgement passes. This confirms that the wait policy Ed∞E_d^\inftyEd∞​ prevents indefinite stalling from discharging a strict contract, while still permitting legitimate transient waits.

Valid input-only operations, ordinary finite prefixes, and terminating computations with finite delay remain positive non-regressions.

8.8 Inspection and proof reuse

Section titled “8.8 Inspection and proof reuse”

The frontier {coord,store}\{\mathrm{coord},\mathrm{store}\}{coord,store} is root-covering and displays both slot protocols. Realization and admission evidence at this frontier transfers finite-safety assurance upward to the root via Corollary 1. Inspecting only the coordinator omits the store path and cannot justify root safety.

This case study illustrates the two human governance tasks formulated in §3.9:

  • Upstream authoring task: A system architect evaluating whether ack(i) requires stronger durability guarantees examines the root intent, the store slot contract, and hypothesis HdurH_{\mathrm{dur}}Hdur​ at the storage substrate boundary. The decision does not require reading or modifying the coordinator’s internal handler definitions.
  • Downstream assessment task: When inspecting an unresolved request, an operator examines the exposed state to distinguish a genuine external wait at the storage flush from an undrained internal output queue or an internal component stall, identifying precisely which environmental assumption or implementation step governs progress.

These scenarios represent concrete governance tasks; they are evaluation designs, not completed empirical human-subject trials.

Suppose the store’s internal representation is modified while its component model, shell protocol, input scope, and slot contract remain unchanged. Once the new handler realization and admission obligations are verified, Corollary 2 allows immediate reuse of existing proofs for Wire⁡(0)\operatorname{Wire}(0)Wire(0), Dec⁡(0)\operatorname{Dec}(0)Dec(0), coordinator compliance, and root satisfaction. Reusing operational progress proofs additionally requires verifying that HwriteH_{\mathrm{write}}Hwrite​ and runtime scheduling premises remain intact. If an update instead alters the substrate crash model, command protocol, or delivery buffering, the affected operands are updated and re-verified accordingly.

9. Related Work

Section titled “9. Related Work”

Transition-system refinement and interfaces. Lynch and Tuttle (1989) separate input, output, and internal actions and make execution composition explicit. De Alfaro and Henzinger (2001) distinguish environmental inputs from component outputs in interface compatibility. Our framework adopts these distinctions within a finite-trace safety setting, pairing trace containment with explicit relative reception and causal delivery obligations to ensure receptive composition. Abadi and Lamport (1991, 1995) study refinement mappings and composition of specifications; Lamport (1994) makes stuttering and temporal interpretation explicit. Here the observation map is restricted enough to prove the needed finite-prefix law directly, without importing a liveness theorem.

Refinement calculi and reactive modeling. UTP designs distinguish feasibility and termination-sensitive meanings from arbitrary relations (Woodcock and Cavalcanti, 2004). Circus separates data and process refinement (Cavalcanti, Sampaio, and Woodcock, 2003), while Event-B organizes initialization, invariants, and refinement obligations (Abrial, 2010). RLNF identifies a structured, pure, terminating handler fragment suitable for automated synthesis and verification. The extensive systems verified by IronFleet (Hawblitzel et al., 2015) highlight the importance of connecting high-level state-machine models to executable distributed code; our calculus formalizes this connection via explicit translation premises and typed runtime obligations.

Shared services. Linearizability provides concurrent operations with a legal sequential interpretation respecting real-time order (Herlihy and Wing, 1990; Filipović et al., 2010). The core calculus captures shared services through single-owner state and explicit parent-mediated serialization, establishing aggregate correctness across concurrent clients. The serialization observed in the shared-counter example is an architectural property of the chosen connector skeleton, rather than an inescapable law of shared mutable state.

Evidence and agent-oriented assurance. Rushby’s Evidential Tool Bus (2005) and the implementations and analyses of Cruanes et al. (2013, 2014) address heterogeneous verification evidence and its logical dependencies. Assurance 2.0’s treatment of defeaters distinguishes challenges to claims, arguments, and evidence (Bloomfield, Netkachova, and Rushby, 2024). CLARISSA develops foundations and automation for assurance cases (Varadarajan et al., 2023); PLACIDUS formalizes assurance-case development for software product lines (Murphy et al., iFM 2024); AssureCode connects developer intent, specifications, and analysis evidence in agentic coding (Murphy et al., 2026). Our contribution integrates these assurance principles with an operational refinement calculus: while structured assurance frameworks organize arguments and defeaters (Bloomfield, Netkachova, and Rushby, 2024; Murphy et al., 2024, 2026), our development DAG provides the formal trace semantics, obligation taxonomy, and typed gates required to verify agent-authored systems.

Provenance, incrementality, and counterexamples. Our provenance and cutoff mechanisms draw upon foundational work in database provenance (Green et al., 2007) and modern build systems (Mokhov et al., 2018). Positive Boolean provenance provides an explanatory model for intent activation paths, rather than requiring an expensive runtime enumeration of all minimal support powersets. Our diagnostic taxonomy builds upon counterexample-guided abstraction refinement (Clarke et al., 2003) to clearly separate abstract model defects from concrete runtime violations.

10. Limitations and Open Problems

Section titled “10. Limitations and Open Problems”

The core calculus proves finite visible-trace safety for its admitted operational fragment. Finite trace inclusion alone permits silence and internal divergence; the operational obligations Ready\mathrm{Ready}Ready and NS\mathrm{NS}NS reject these covered failure modes separately. Genuine, indefinitely unresolved external prerequisites are admitted only where the accepted contract’s wait policy explicitly allows them (e∈Ed∞e \in E_d^\inftye∈Ed∞​), and such states remain visible as pending. This operational condition does not guarantee eventual success, a terminal response under arbitrary environment failure, or hard real-time deadlines. General progress-preserving abstraction and component substitution require dedicated temporal refinement theorems; the finite trace safety theorems do not supply them.

The example’s scheduling premise Hexec0H_{\mathrm{exec}}^0Hexec0​ is an explicit per-use weak-fairness assumption on a finite acyclic continuation, not a proved property of a host operating system scheduler. Weak fairness concerns eventual continuous enabling, whereas strong fairness concerns repeated enabling; neither follows from finite trace containment or terminating leaf handlers. No general fairness theorem is proved.

RLNF excludes hidden effects and unproved within-handler divergence, but does not prevent connector-level communication deadlocks if slot contracts permit circular waits. State-indexed reception restricts deployment inputs; it is not global input-enabledness. Sharing restrictions exclude unmediated mutable aliases and do not provide a general concurrent-history substitution theorem. Adding those behaviors requires new boundary semantics and proofs rather than a broader interpretation of an existing inclusion.

Symbolic state and data domains may be infinite. Deterministic-monitor simulation completeness is an existence theorem, not an algorithm for automatically synthesizing invariants or ranking functions. Context consistency, physical substrate fidelity, source-to-elaboration translation, and publication correctness can remain trusted premises. Contract precision limits what a parent can establish: a Top slot cannot carry a nontrivial durability promise by itself.

The worked example is a single-request model, not a production storage implementation or crash-recovery protocol. Furthermore, runtime scheduling correspondence and interactive visual inspection interfaces are not mechanized in this paper. The paper makes no empirical claim that the workflow reduces agent error rates, cognitive load, review cost, or proof effort. Demonstrating those benefits requires implementations, representative tasks, and measured comparisons with explicitly scoped acceptance criteria.

11. Conclusion

Section titled “11. Conclusion”

A refinement DAG separates what a boundary promises, how its children establish that promise, and why the available evidence applies. In service of five root purposes—realizing committed behavior, preserving authority over governing meaning, keeping justified change local, reducing human governance context, and keeping assurance accountable to evidence—the calculus establishes a rigorous boundary for agent-authored systems.

RLNF supplies executable leaf semantics, homomorphic observations connect traces across interfaces, deterministic monitors support complete simulation reasoning, and single-owner state locates interaction obligations. Guarded wiring closes the composition seam, while protected contracts and the incremental frame theorem enable exact-operand evidence reuse across versioned evolution without silently changing accepted meaning. Separately verified operational obligations govern input reception, operational readiness, and contract-relative non-silent response, distinguishing permitted terminal outcomes from genuine, inspectable external waits. The resulting guarantee is conditional, compositional, and explicit about its operational, environmental, and trusted boundaries.

A.3 Packet Decomposition

Section titled “A.3 Packet Decomposition”

Consider a finite path from (s0,[])(s_0,[])(s0​,[]) in elab⁡(D)\operatorname{elab}(D)elab(D). Every input step starts with an empty pending list. It selects exactly one enabled handler result (s′,w)(s',w)(s′,w), after which only the successive heads of www can be emitted until the list empties. Induction on the number of input steps partitions the path into complete packets and, possibly, one last input with an initial segment of its output word. Because that remaining word is finite, drain it without any further input. The resulting trace is a member of Packets⁡(D)\operatorname{Packets}(D)Packets(D) extending the original trace. A path with no input is the zero-step path and has trace ϵ\epsilonϵ. Thus the left side is contained in the right.

Conversely, take a packet word from an enabled finite handler chain. Starting at (s0,[])(s_0,[])(s0​,[]), apply each chain input rule and then drain its listed outputs. The handler’s next state is exactly the next chain state, so this constructs an execution of the whole word. For any prefix of the word, stop this execution after the corresponding event. Empty outputs require no drain transitions; the empty prefix requires no transitions. Thus every prefix is an elaborated trace. □\square□

The lemma accounts for intermediate prefixes occurring between successive output emissions, precisely reflecting microstep evaluation while preserving the invariant that input dispatch occurs only when pending output buffers are exhausted.

A.5 Deterministic Contract Simulation Equivalence

Section titled “A.5 Deterministic Contract Simulation Equivalence”

Let BBB have one initial state q0q_0q0​, no hidden transitions, partial deterministic β\betaβ, and every reachable state accepting. For a word www admitted by BBB, let β^(q0,w)\widehat\beta(q_0,w)β​(q0​,w) denote its unique reached state. Extend λ\lambdaλ by erasing source internal labels.

A.6 Finite-control progress proof for the durable acknowledgement example

Section titled “A.6 Finite-control progress proof for the durable acknowledgement example”

We formalize the four-step progress proof for the composite execution witness N0N_0N0​ under scheduling premise Hexec0H_{\mathrm{exec}}^0Hexec0​ and write premise HwriteH_{\mathrm{write}}Hwrite​.

Let π∈CExec⁡0(N0,ω)\pi \in \operatorname{CExec}_0(N_0,\omega)π∈CExec0​(N0​,ω) be a maximal execution, and let request req(i) occur at step k0k_0k0​, activating duty ddd. The composite reachable state space is finite and acyclic. Every owned transition is labeled by an action in Owned⁡0\operatorname{Owned}_0Owned0​.

  1. Absence of infinite owned executions: Since the reachable control graph contains no directed cycles of owned transitions, π\piπ cannot contain infinitely many consecutive owned transitions.
  2. Readiness on pending states: By the configuration case split in §8.6.1, every reachable pending configuration sss where neither Wd,write(i)W_{d,\mathrm{write}(i)}Wd,write(i)​ nor Wd,flush(i)W_{d,\mathrm{flush}(i)}Wd,flush(i)​ holds enables an owned continuation transition s→owned(d)s′s \xrightarrow{\mathrm{owned}(d)} s'sowned(d)​s′.
  3. Write phase: If π\piπ reaches write wait Wd,write(i)W_{d,\mathrm{write}(i)}Wd,write(i)​ (shell state hW(i)hW(i)hW(i)), premise HwriteH_{\mathrm{write}}Hwrite​ ensures that the matching response write_ok(i) is emitted after finite delay. Under Hexec0H_{\mathrm{exec}}^0Hexec0​, the store cannot indefinitely postpone dispatching this enabled response.
  4. Flush phase and disjunctive closure: Following write completion, the acyclic continuation enables Cmd.fsync(i). Under Hexec0H_{\mathrm{exec}}^0Hexec0​, this command is synchronized, reaching flush wait configuration hPending(i)hPending(i)hPending(i) where Wd,flush(i)W_{d,\mathrm{flush}(i)}Wd,flush(i)​ holds.
    • Case 4a: If the substrate shell emits fsync_ok(i) or fsync_fail(i), the enabled store handler transitions to state Done with pending outputs. Under Hexec0H_{\mathrm{exec}}^0Hexec0​, each enabled drain transition is executed in finite steps, reaching root emission of ack(i) or fail(i). This witnesses terminal outcome DdD_dDd​, satisfying the first disjunct FDd\mathbf{F} D_dFDd​.
    • Case 4b: If the substrate shell emits no response, no owned transition is enabled. The execution stutters indefinitely in hPending(i)hPending(i)hPending(i), where Wd,flush(i)W_{d,\mathrm{flush}(i)}Wd,flush(i)​ holds globally thereafter. Because flush(i)∈Ed∞\mathrm{flush}(i) \in E_d^\inftyflush(i)∈Ed∞​, this witnesses the second disjunct ∃e∈Ed∞. FGWd,e\exists e\in E_d^\infty.\ \mathbf{F}\mathbf{G} W_{d,e}∃e∈Ed∞​. FGWd,e​.

Therefore, π⊨G(Pd⇒[FDd∨∃e∈Ed∞. FGWd,e])\pi \models \mathbf{G}(P_d \Rightarrow [\mathbf{F} D_d \lor \exists e\in E_d^\infty.\ \mathbf{F}\mathbf{G} W_{d,e}])π⊨G(Pd​⇒[FDd​∨∃e∈Ed∞​. FGWd,e​]), completing the proof of condition (NS)(\mathrm{NS})(NS). □\square□
